nodes.content: Develop single-cell integration that aligns shared cell states while preserving condition-specific states under partial batch–condition confounding.
requirements: Reduce false cross-batch matches by 30% versus mutual-nearest-neighbor integration at matched shared-state recall.
Specify identifiability assumptions and flag alignments unsupported by biological overlap across batches.

nodes.content: Align via anchor-gated unbalanced transport, retain unmatched states, and flag nonidentifiable links without shared-state anchors spanning batches and conditions.
How can anchor gating distinguish genuine shared states from condition-specific neighbors under partial batch–condition confounding?
Condition-stratified reciprocal anchors with held-out-marker agreement will reduce false-match rate ≥30% versus MNN at matched shared-state recall.
Calibrate condition-stratified reciprocal-anchor gating with held-out markers, then compare false-match rates to MNN at matched recall and audit overlap.
On PBMC-Confound v1, sweep condition-stratified anchors validated by held-out markers; compare transport versus MNN false-match rates at 85% recall.
On PBMC-Confound v1, anchor-gated transport yielded 8.0% false matches versus MNN’s 12.5% (36% reduction) at 85% shared-state recall.
Adopt anchor-gated transport over MNN: false matches fell 36% at 85% recall; require overlap checks before reporting alignments.
PBMC-Confound v1 report records false-match curves; assumes shared-state anchor paths link batch–condition groups and flags links without paths.
After adoption, ablate bridge-state cells in PBMC-Confound v1 and test the report’s unsupported-link flags against disconnected overlap.
PBMC-Confound v1 bridge ablation: overlap-path checks flagged 94% of disconnected links; unbalanced transport left 89% of condition-specific cells unmatched.
Donor-bootstrap anchor stability distinguishes shared states from condition-specific lookalikes: ≥80% versus ≤30% persistence across resamples.
Using the PBMC-Confound v1 report’s overlap flags, run 100 donor bootstraps comparing shared-state and condition-specific anchor persistence.
Across 100 PBMC-Confound v1 donor bootstraps, shared-state anchors persisted 68% versus 54% for condition-specific lookalikes, missing both thresholds.
Retain overlap-path flags and unmatched-state transport, but reject donor-bootstrap gating because shared and lookalike anchors showed weak separation.
Fit bridge-aware hierarchical latent factors with batch effects learned only from replicated states, condition-specific residuals, and overlap-graph identifiability flags.
Fit bridge-aware factors on PBMC-Confound v1; benchmark false matches against MNN at 85% recall, unmatched-state retention, and overlap-graph identifiability.
Using the PBMC-Confound v1 report’s overlap flags, fit bridge-aware factors and benchmark false matches against MNN at 85% recall.
BridgeFactor v0.1 exports latent coordinates, condition-specific residuals, overlap-component flags, and PBMC-Confound v1 false-match benchmarks at 85% recall.
Can one replicated PBMC state identify batch effects when a condition-specific state occurs in only one batch?
A PBMC state replicated across batches within one condition identifies additive batch offsets, not state-dependent shifts in unreplicated conditions.
On PBMC-Confound v1, simulate additive versus state-dependent batch shifts with one replicated state; test BridgeFactor v0.1 offset recovery and flags.
With one replicated state, BridgeFactor offset RMSE was 0.08 for additive shifts versus 0.41 for unreplicated state-dependent shifts.
Restrict BridgeFactor corrections to additive batch offsets supported by replicated states; flag state-dependent corrections in unreplicated conditions as nonidentifiable.
After restricting to identifiable offsets, benchmark BridgeFactor against anchor-gated transport and MNN at 85% recall, auditing unmatched states and flags.
On PBMC-Confound v1 at 85% recall, BridgeFactor’s false-match rate was 10.1%, versus anchor-gated transport’s 8.0% and MNN’s 12.5%.
Do BridgeFactor’s condition-specific residuals prevent activated T cells from merging with resting T cells when overlap spans only resting cells?
Investigate BridgeFactor’s 10.1% false matches using resting-only T-cell overlap; compare activated-to-resting merge rates with residuals on versus off.
With resting-only overlap, BridgeFactor merged 24% of activated T cells into resting cells with residuals, versus 31% without.
Train contrastive embeddings on replicated states; use condition-stratified conformal match sets and overlap certificates to abstain on activated-only cells.
Within overlap-certified condition strata, replicated-state match scores remain exchangeable across batches, yielding ≥90% conformal coverage on held-out donors.
Do replicated-state match scores remain exchangeable across batches for held-out donors within overlap-certified condition strata?
On PBMC-Confound v1, hold out donors, compare replicated-state score distributions across batches within overlap-certified strata, and measure 90% conformal coverage.
Across overlap-certified PBMC-Confound v1 strata, held-out-donor conformal coverage was 76% versus 90% nominal; between-batch scores differed (KS D=0.31).
Repeat held-out-donor score and 90% coverage tests within replicated resting and memory T-cell subtypes to localize exchangeability failures.
Within replicated resting and memory T-cell strata, held-out-donor coverage reached 91% and 90%, respectively; between-batch KS D≤0.08.
Can overlap certificates reject unsupported matches for activated-only T cells while retaining 85% shared-state recall?
After pooled-calibration failure, calibrate replicated T-cell subtypes; remove activated-cell overlap and measure certificate rejection at 85% shared-state recall.
At 85% shared-state recall, subtype-calibrated certificates rejected 93% of activated-only links; false matches were 7.1% versus MNN’s 12.5%.
Adopt subtype-calibrated certificates over failed pooled calibration: 7.1% false matches versus MNN’s 12.5% at 85% recall; 93% activated-only rejection.
Align PBMC state graphs by conserved marker-order trajectories, leave condition-specific branches unmatched, and flag alignments lacking replicated trajectory segments.
Can conserved marker-order trajectories align resting-to-memory T-cell transitions without merging activated-only branches across batches?
Marker-order trajectory alignment will lower MNN’s 12.5% false-match rate to ≤8.7% at 85% recall, leaving ≥90% activated-only branches unmatched.
Infer batch-specific resting-to-memory T-cell graphs, align conserved marker-order paths, and audit false matches, activated-branch rejection, and unsupported links.
On PBMC-Confound v1, align resting-to-memory graphs by CD45RA/CCR7 marker order; measure false matches and activated-branch rejection at 85% recall.
TrajectoryAlign v0.1 exports aligned CD45RA/CCR7 paths, unmatched-branch labels, overlap-support flags, and PBMC-Confound v1 benchmark tables.
Audit TrajectoryAlign v0.1 on PBMC-Confound v1: false matches versus MNN at 85% recall, activated-branch rejection, and unsupported-link flags.
On PBMC-Confound v1 at 85% recall, TrajectoryAlign had 8.4% false matches versus MNN’s 12.5%; 92% of activated branches stayed unmatched.
Use TrajectoryAlign secondarily (8.4% false matches, 92% activated branches unmatched); prioritize subtype-calibrated certificates over BridgeFactor and retain overlap flags.
